title: T016 bounded BFF OIDC session implementation is proof-ready but human-gated
summary: The Nuxt BFF T016 slice now has provider-neutral authorization-code/PKCE, state and nonce binding, opaque server-side sessions, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, CSRF enforcement, canonical role denial, logout revocation hooks and local OIDC stub proof. It is intentionally not production-activated or merged.

claims.text: Tests-first T016 auth-session coverage initially failed only at the absent session-service runtime boundary, then passed after the bounded implementation was added.

The local OIDC stub verifies a signed RS256 JWT through JWKS, checks issuer/audience/nonce/roles, exchanges the authorization code server-side and revokes refresh/access tokens without exposing bearer material to the browser session view.
Published anonymous SSR remains available when auth is unconfigured; protected routes fail closed and provider outage returns a safe authentication error.
The next required action is human threat-model review plus exact-head remote CI/Security and protected merge/checkbox gating; do not activate a production IdP or durable session store in this lane.

blocks: T016 protected merge and checkbox reconciliation

decision.context: T016 must provide optional login/session support without making anonymous Courtside TW reading depend on Web3 or an external identity provider.
decision.chosen: Use a provider-neutral BFF authorization-code/PKCE boundary with server-side token storage, opaque cookies, CSRF and explicit local/CI stub parity; fail closed for protected routes while public SSR remains anonymous.
alternatives: Store access or refresh tokens in browser storage.
Make login a prerequisite for public article reading.
Contact or configure a production IdP and durable session store in the implementation lane.
tradeoffs: The local/CI memory store makes the proof deterministic but is deliberately rejected for production activation.
Explicit revocation and session rotation add server-side state but reduce bearer and fixation risk.
The provider-neutral port leaves durable store/provider wiring for a separate human-approved gate.
decision.invalidation: If the T015 issuer/audience/role contract, public anonymous-read policy, threat model or session-store decision changes, mark this record needs_update and stop before widening T016.
